content:
Hi all,

Inspired by erdosproblems.com, I built a preprint server allowing for AI-generated papers, with certificates issued by humans to signal quality. There seems to be a need for new mathematical infrastructure, and I believe this kind of website — which I view as a crossover between arXiv, erdosproblems.com and merely-true— could complement traditional publication channels.

Here’s a prototype. There are only dummy papers so far, but the core features are live: you can create accounts, submit papers and review the work of others. Feel free to try it out — I can delete any data afterwards if you want, just let me know. :slight_smile:

One possible certificate is ‘Formal verification in Lean 4’. Does the current certificate specification make sense?

Also feel free to share thoughts on this project more broadly, or let me know if you’d want to be involved. Could a platform like this become a useful piece of mathematical infrastructure? And if so, what design decisions matter most?

Thanks for your time. :blush:
Do you require authors to comply with some Creative Commons licence? Also, do you expect DOI's or SWid's to be attached to submissions?

Neither is currently implemented, but these are good ideas. I could add a licence selector to the 'Submit paper' page (as arXiv). Automatically assigning DOIs seems trickier (and costs money, I believe).

Why this stipulation: "A paper may have zero human authors."

I think this cuts out a large group of people who use AI in one or more forms but do not depend on it entirely for either the production of the paper or the production of the content itself.

To be clear, entirely human-authored papers are very welcome too -- this site can host anything from human-written to AI-written. But yes, I should make this more explicit! We can adjust author policies later, depending on the content.
''Create an account" gives a 404 for me.
Thanks for the bug report Ralf, it's fixed now.
Nice! This is great @Isabel Dahlgren , I love the idea of having certificates which attests to quality! It is worth mentioning parallel arXiv which is a similar home for AI-generated papers.
Oh, silly me. I read that completely backwards didn't I.

Isabel Dahlgren said:

One possible certificate is ‘Formal verification in Lean 4’. Does the current certificate specification make sense?

I think it only makes sense if the only imports to a Challenge.lean are Mathlib (or maybe a slightly larger "blessed" set of repositories. (Or maybe only repositories / files that have been audited via some public auditing system, that I know people are thinking about...?) Otherwise people will just write Challenge files that import thousands of lines of garbage, and it hasn't helped the auditing process at all.
(And just to be clear --- this preprint server itself is off-topic on this forum, only the Lean certification aspect is on-topic here.)
This is great input @Kim Morrison! I've now updated the certificate specification. Any imports beyond Mathlib need to be justified.

In case anyone comes across this thread, I’ve now given the site a proper domain: https://projectdiderot.com. I've also incorporated feedback from you and others.

You're very welcome to start uploading papers or writeups, written with or without AI. To share additional comments, you can always DM me. Thanks!
